t.4.35.1: Thus addressed by Tārā with words that were courteous and in accord with dharma, Saumitri, gentle by nature, accepted that speech.
t.4.35.2: When those words had been accepted, the lord of the monkey hosts cast off his very great fear of Lakṣmaṇa, as one casts off a wet garment.
t.4.35.4: Then Sugrīva, the foremost of all the monkeys, spoke courteous words to Lakṣmaṇa of formidable strength, gladdening him greatly.
t.4.35.3: Then Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, tore apart the great, many-stranded, colourful garland that hung about his neck, and he became free of intoxication.
t.4.35.5: My lost fortune and glory, and the lasting kingdom of the monkeys, O Saumitri, all this has been regained by me through the grace of Rāma.
t.4.35.7: The righteous-souled Rāghava will recover Sītā and will slay Rāvaṇa by his own might, with me as merely his helper.
t.4.35.6: O hero, subduer of enemies, who is able to repay such valour of that god, renowned through his own deeds?
t.4.35.8: For the duty of an ally is owed to him, by whom seven great trees, the mountain, and the very earth were pierced with a single arrow.
t.4.35.9: O Lakṣmaṇa, he by whose sound, as he draws his bow, the earth with its mountains is made to tremble, what need indeed has he of allies?
t.4.35.11: If I, your servant, have transgressed in any way, whether out of trust or out of affection, it should be forgiven me; there is no one who does not err.
t.4.35.10: O bull among men, I shall follow the lord of men as he goes forth to slay his enemy Rāvaṇa together with his followers.
t.4.35.12: As the great-souled Sugrīva was speaking thus, Lakṣmaṇa became pleased, and with affection he spoke these words.
t.4.35.13: O Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, in every way my brother is well protected, having you as his protector, especially as you are so courteous.
t.4.35.15: And with you as his ally, O Sugrīva, the valiant Rāma will soon slay his enemies in battle; there is no doubt about this.
t.4.35.14: O Sugrīva, given the might that is yours and the supreme purity that is yours, you are worthy to enjoy the unsurpassed splendour of the kingdom of the monkeys.
t.4.35.16: O Sugrīva, your words are fitting and proper for one who knows dharma, who is grateful, and who never turns back in battles.
t.4.35.17: Who else, knowing the faults and having the capacity, is fit to speak thus, apart from my elder brother and you, O best of monkeys?
t.4.35.18: You are equal to Rāma in valor and in strength, O bull among monkeys, an ally granted to him by the gods for a long time.
t.4.35.19: But, O hero, come out from here quickly with me, and console your friend, who is grieving over the abduction of his wife.
t.4.35.20: And since, having heard the words of Rāma, who was overwhelmed by grief, I spoke harsh words to you, you ought to forgive that as well.
